sections.title: A soul is not a map coordinate
sections.establishedSourceReading: The original account places mortal soul formation near the prison and emphasizes agency. It later describes soul passage at the Argent Gate and a Gate of Gentle Departures. The Player appendix expressly calls its cosmography mortal belief. Those accounts do not yet give one exhaustive route for every dead identity.
sections.proposedProcedure: Retain each account with its time and authority. For an actual return, use the source’s willing identity, body/formation, location, clock and real blocker rules. Do not add a guessed afterlife destination or true-name prerequisite to True Resurrection. A soul’s transition is not automatically the cessation described in Matrix Tier Ten.
sections.remainingDecisions: The campaign epoch, complete afterlife jurisdiction and the relationship between the Argent Gate and mortal Shadow Conclave claims remain for source-based discussion.

sections.title: Research records what was learned
sections.establishedSourceReading: The owner requires deciphering through Research across multiple Descent libraries. Core Matrix research requires the primary researcher’s own high ranks in five disciplines and cross-reference among drops, libraries, mechanisms and seasonal change. The secondary Instruments guide supplies clock examples, not the completed Equation puzzle.
sections.proposedProcedure: NEW record each discovery’s physical source, exact claim, translation evidence, researcher, prerequisites, elapsed work and demonstrated usable understanding. Keep a copied inscription distinct from understanding it. Duplicate copies of one claim do not become independent corroboration or new discoveries. Progress should reveal something usable in play as well as preserve its deeper interpretation for the Director.
sections.remainingDecisions: Define high ranks, the Research skill/team interface, actual library sites, clue dependencies, time/cost/check rules and completion criteria with GPT. Do not select six universal ticks, five fragments, a single die roll or a fixed equation variant merely because an earlier example used one.

sections.title: Keep the two causes of taint visible
sections.establishedSourceReading: The owner gives two causes: functional knowledge of the Equation, and voices/proximity to the Old Ones at Descent level5 onward. No arithmetic combination, seven-stage scale or automatic mapping to Corrupted/Unity Exposure was chosen.
sections.proposedProcedure: NEW record the actual knowledge event or actual exposure event separately, with the affected identity and its source. Record any resulting condition or track change only under an explicitly defined rule. Knowledge is not required for proximity taint, and owning a manuscript alone does not prove functional knowledge. Neither record proves allegiance, guilt or a named Old One identity.
sections.remainingDecisions: Progression, doses, thresholds, resistance, recovery, transfer and the meaning of falling remain open. An undefined interface is not permission to invent immunity or to impose an unsupported penalty.

sections.title: Pact attention and Hunt initiation are separate decisions
sections.establishedSourceReading: Core forbidden magic can create evidence, attention or Pact pursuit even on a successful cast. The Matrix describes the Warden and automatons as guardians of the system. The owner’s final-death rule begins once a Hunt is initiated; the exact initiating condition and hunters are not named.
sections.proposedProcedure: NEW use a written Hunt initiation event: affected identity, actual triggering violation, enforcing authority, evidence, start time and the mechanical consequences communicated to the player. Preserve the distinction between investigation, suspicion and an active Hunt. Define what each pursuer actually knows and can do; do not grant all NPCs omniscience or equate every ordinary patrol with the Hunt.
sections.remainingDecisions: Choose the exact violation threshold, recognition process, notice, pursuit roster, escalation and lawful ending. Original-source priority does not authorize inventing a universal automaton police force.

sections.title: Resolve survival before deciding that death occurred
sections.establishedSourceReading: The current life interface distinguishes HP floors, healing a surviving zero-HP creature, would-die replacement, actual resurrection and companion reconstruction. Phoenix Rebirth targets a living ally; Ritual Ward replaces eligible pending death. Neither is an ordinary after-death resurrection.
sections.proposedProcedure: PROPOSED Hunt reading: retain each otherwise legal pre-death survival operation. Resolve its exact source timing and costs; if it prevents actual death, the character remains hunted and alive. Do not call Hunt status an unpreventable-death tag without an express rule. A later actual death still invokes the Hunt consequence. This proposal needs GPT agreement on the owner’s wording.
sections.remainingDecisions: Confirm fatal Wound, Instant Death, third failure and lethal-track interactions separately through the existing ordered life interface. Do not generalize the narrow ordinary Death Ward into Ritual Ward’s broader replacement.

sections.title: An actual hunted death is normally final
sections.establishedSourceReading: The owner states that a Hunt makes the character hardcore and death final, then allows very limited exceptions including extremely rare Divine/Abyssal intervention. Ordinary return abilities cannot provide a routine exception.
sections.proposedProcedure: PROPOSED apply the consequence to actual death during an active Hunt regardless of whether the final cause was a hunter, a fall or another hazard. Record the death identity and Hunt together. Ordinary Resurrection, True Resurrection and class revival do not bypass that consequence merely by meeting their usual body/window requirements. Transporting remains, releasing Soul Bind or changing appearance does not itself settle the Hunt. Any authorized exception must say exactly what it overrides.
sections.remainingDecisions: Confirm the all-causes interpretation and the relationship between ending a Hunt before death, pardon after death and an extraordinary return. No absolute ban on Divine/Abyssal intervention is reinstated.

sections.title: An intervention needs its own written terms
sections.establishedSourceReading: The owner allows extremely rare Divine/Abyssal intervention without a chosen list, frequency, price, trigger or sponsor. A class feature named Divine Rebirth only modifies an already successful Cleric resurrection. Infernal resurrection clauses exist in the fiction but are not universal permission.
sections.proposedProcedure: NEW proposal: each exceptional intervention is an explicit campaign event with a named competent intervener, established reason, eligibility, timing, precise overridden barrier, body/identity result, willingness, price or obligation, retained consequences and limit on future use. State whether it ends the Hunt, permits one return while the Hunt continues, or changes a different consequence. Mere divine tags, spell rank, paid temple service or an ordinary signed contract do not create this event.
sections.remainingDecisions: The actual exceptional routes and their scarcity need authorship and joint review. This record format does not approve an intervener, invent a price, force a player to accept, or make intervention a guaranteed rescue.

sections.title: Cleansing and diagnosis retain their real scope
sections.establishedSourceReading: Corruption Cleanse can remove an eligible ordinary Corrupted record without removing knowledge, a major/protected cause, Unity Exposure or an intrinsic curse. Corruption Ward helps existing qualifying saves but creates no new save. Detection and Insight use actual records and protection rules.
sections.proposedProcedure: Keep these benefits when their predicates are satisfied. NEW do not treat a cured symptom as automatic loss of functional understanding, cancellation of a recorded Hunt or destruction of a separate source. Conversely, do not declare all taint immune to cleansing by default. Define which records the taint system actually creates and which existing spell predicates can inspect, protect or remove them. Corruption Insight must answer honestly within its known/protected fields; secrecy alone is not a new protection.
sections.remainingDecisions: Specify source tags, knowledge versus condition recovery and actual protections before applying detection or cure. Higher-rank Purge, Immunity and Purification remain pending; their stronger source wording must be reviewed rather than quietly reduced to lower Cleanse.

sections.title: Returning a body does not erase history
sections.establishedSourceReading: Existing resurrection retains Wounds, Corruption, spent resources and legal/body claims. Corpse-local denial differs from an identity/soul blocker. The new Hunt rule creates an additional unresolved interface; it does not convert every legal claim into a soul prison.
sections.proposedProcedure: Use one continuing identity and one actual death/return event. Retain valid histories and resolve the actual source’s permitted body or formation mode. NEW require an explicit cause and procedure before treating a legal debt or contract as a return barrier. Keep the carrier of remains, owner of equipment, legal claimant and bound soul separate. Source-specific blocked activation versus later failed paid resolution retains its existing cost rule.
sections.remainingDecisions: Complete any actual infernal clause or claim before using it to prevent return. Do not infer that all contracts survived refraction unchanged or that a former jurisdiction owns every present soul.

sections.title: Copies and rewinds do not supply an unreviewed escape
sections.establishedSourceReading: Clone is still pending. Arcane Clone is an illusionary copy, with an unadopted procedure that excludes soul transfer. Full Time Loop remains unavailable; its bounded kernel separately restores life-state and conserves certain histories/memories.
sections.proposedProcedure: Keep those availability boundaries. NEW require an explicit temporal policy for functional knowledge, both taint causes, Hunt initiation, Pact enforcement and any exceptional intervention before a scene involving them is admitted to a future complete Time Loop. A generic claim that temporal restoration is not resurrection is insufficient to waive the owner’s Hunt consequence. A proposed temporal policy must also account for who remembers what.
sections.remainingDecisions: The conference must recommend an exact policy rather than assert that everything rewinds or nothing does. This draft does not disable ordinary source effects already covered by their actual rules, complete Time Loop, or grant Clone a procedure.

sections.title: Reveal consequences without handing out the cosmology
sections.establishedSourceReading: The Player appendix distinguishes mortal belief from objective history. Current information spells report only their allowed facts; Soul Mark ends at death and does not track a detached soul. The Director guidance supports earned, distributed clues and intelligible bargain terms.
sections.proposedProcedure: NEW maintain a player record of perceived clues, understood claims and announced mechanical consequences, alongside the Director’s source/cause record. A player can know that a Hunt has made death normally final without being told every cosmic identity or the full Equation. Research should supply observable progress and actionable choices; hidden knowledge is not a reason to fabricate divination failure.
sections.remainingDecisions: Define how the character learns about the danger, what signs precede the Hunt and what remains hidden. Keep public reliable knowledge and the Q6 ceiling intact.

sections.title: Requirements for a playable chapter
sections.establishedSourceReading: The source comparison supports a coherent distinction among knowledge, taint, conditions, pursuit, death and extraordinary return. It does not yet supply a complete puzzle or all the procedures needed to run those consequences.
sections.proposedProcedure: Ask GPT to confirm or correct SH-01–11, propose finite solutions for the open interfaces and identify any original passage that supersedes this reading. Every new threshold, clock, cost, agency restriction or exception must be labeled authored design. Bring unresolved owner-level cosmology conflicts back as precise alternatives after exhausting the existing sources.
sections.remainingDecisions: Completion requires the actual library/clue chain, research progression, taint rules, Hunt triggers/pursuers/ending, rare interventions, death/temporal interfaces, player warnings and worked campaign examples. This draft closes none of those domains by itself.

casebook.situation: A porter carries an unread copy through a library.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Do not infer functional understanding from ownership. Separately evaluate any actual voice/proximity exposure.

casebook.situation: A creature hears the voices below Descent level5 without having found a manuscript.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: The owner allows proximity taint independently of research. No automatic numerical amount or guilt follows.

casebook.situation: A hunted ally would fall from positive HP to0 under an otherwise eligible ordinary Death Ward.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Proposed: resolve the existing floor; it prevents that drop, does not end the Hunt and supplies no outright-death protection.

casebook.situation: A hunted ally suffers a fatal Wound while an eligible Ritual Ward is active.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Proposed: use the existing would-die replacement window; Hunt status alone is not yet an explicit unpreventable-death source. Confirm with GPT.

casebook.situation: A hunted identity actually dies and an ally offers ordinary True Resurrection.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: The owner disallows routine return. Meeting the usual seven-day/bodyless requirements is not itself an extraordinary intervention.

casebook.situation: A Cleric calls Divine Rebirth a divine exception.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Its actual card modifies a successful Cleric return; its name alone does not authorize a Hunt exception.

casebook.situation: Soul Bind expires after a hunted death, or the body is moved out of a denial zone.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: The actual corresponding blocker ends. Proposed: this does not by itself end the separate Hunt consequence.

casebook.situation: A researcher receives Corruption Cleanse while retaining functional knowledge.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Remove an actual eligible ordinary Corrupted record. The spell does not erase knowledge or a major source. Proposed: Hunt/knowledge records persist unless an explicit rule changes them.

casebook.situation: A warded researcher gains taint under a future rule that grants no saving throw.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Corruption Ward cannot manufacture a save. First decide whether that exact future effect is tagged Corruption and what its procedure is.

casebook.situation: Corruption Insight examines a record whose type is known but cause is undefined.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Report the actual type and Indeterminate cause. Do not invent the Old God, its location or the researcher’s guilt.

casebook.situation: The same translated page is copied ten times.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Proposed: copies preserve evidence but do not become ten independent discoveries or corroborating sources.

casebook.situation: A successor inherits an archive but lacks the primary researcher’s required disciplines.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Core permits inherited archive knowledge while requiring personal Matrix research qualifications; define the missing numeric ranks before adjudicating eligibility.

casebook.situation: A player cites the Shadow Conclave as proof that the Raven Regent owns every dead soul.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: The appendix presents mortal testimony. Preserve that belief without promoting it to a universal objective rule.

casebook.situation: A proposed high-rank Purification is invoked to erase all taint and cancel the Hunt.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: The spell is pending. Its permanent-removal wording needs its own full review and an explicit taint/Hunt interface; no automatic permission or universal immunity is supplied here.

casebook.situation: A caster calls an Arcane Clone a spare soul vessel.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: The source specifies an illusionary copy. The unadopted draft denies biological clone/death replacement/soul transfer. Ordinary Clone remains separately pending.

casebook.situation: A Time Loop is proposed after forbidden understanding or Hunt initiation.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Full Time Loop remains unavailable. A future admitted implementation needs explicit knowledge/taint/Hunt and memory policies; its name cannot bypass the unresolved interface.

casebook.situation: An abyssal patron offers one exceptional return with a specific obligation.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Proposed: record authority, eligibility, exact overridden barrier, willingness, price, retained consequences and whether the Hunt ends or continues. This example grants no actual intervention.

casebook.situation: A hunted character dies in an accident rather than at a hunter’s hands.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Proposed all-causes reading: actual death during the Hunt invokes the same normal-finality rule. Confirm the owner’s wording with GPT.

casebook.situation: A secret is protected only because the Director wants it to remain mysterious.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Existing information abilities still receive honest answers within their scope; actual source-specific protection can withhold its covered facts. A secret alone is no new immunity.

casebook.situation: A six-tick example is presented as the canonical complete Equation.
casebook.expectedForDiscussion: Instruments gives research-clock examples. It neither chooses the owner’s inscription variant nor establishes a universal fragment count or completed solution.

MORTAL_ORIGIN.verbatim: Yet every new branch increased complexity, presenting gaps through which hush might seep. To address risk, Pattern drafted great schema linking all plane frequencies into overarching cadence. Courage and Sorrow acted as pillars anchoring farthest extremes, while Contradiction wove tolerance for paradox into central hub. Law sealed plan with charter recognized by Pact yet free of Asmodeus seal. This grand map would guide future calibrations. While grand realms found shape, fragments of Source energy near prison coalesced into first mortal souls on world called Aethel. These souls shimmered fragile, ignorant of cosmic war, yet their resonance chimed perfectly with newborn planes. A child’s fearless laughter resonated with Courage pillar in Bastion. An elder’s whispered regret drifted through Sorrow’s gardens in Veiled Expanse. A scholar’s restless curiosity soared across Boundless Void.

MORTAL_AGENCY.verbatim: The Choir observed with awe. Here existed beings neither devil nor angel, neither demon nor Choir. Their choices might tip balances with astonishing efficiency because they lacked predetermined bias. Calan’thir proposed gift: grant mortals subtle attunement pathways so they could draw inspiration from planes without losing agency. Transition opened faint channels, guiding dreamers into Radiant archipelagos, guiding philosophers toward Thought constellations, guiding adventurers into Crucible chambers. Asmodeus also observed. Mortal souls represented fresh currency. Seeds of infernal law could flourish in hearts eager for certainty. He tasked contracts wraiths to wander dreamscapes, offering hope in exchange for vow. Thus conflict extended downward, but under Choir surveillance coercion remained limited. The stage set for ages of guided free will. When all dust settled, the Divine Pact pulsed with deeper timbre. Fire, shadow, dream, and thought now sang four part counterpoint around seal. Their endless discourse radiated energies that lulled Ul’nak to deeper slumber while feeding Spiral motion. The Choir maintained vigilant harmony. Asmodeus directed infernal war from afar. Demons beat drums of unending revolt. Mortals awoke to skies colored by unseen planes.

ARGENT_PASSAGE.verbatim: So the universe waited, balancing on breath between note and echo, while the Sentient Pact listened to itself inside every vow. Nine nights after the awakening archon Quorilith observed anomaly within the Argent Gate. Normally the Gate shifts hue with passage of souls, violet during departures, indigo during arrivals. That night it rippled in rings of alternating pearl and onyx, a pattern never logged. Quorilith opened his crystalline sigil book. Every page filled at once with identical phrase written in sigils of all seven Choir chords entwined, impossible by mortal script. Phrase read, in meaning rather than uttered word, “Balance is choice remembered.”

GENTLE_DEPARTURES.verbatim: Shaenira composed Lament Festival, annual convergence where sorrow is sung until transformed into gratitude. Bardic troupes, shamans, oracles joined, turning grief into kinetic sculpture that floated skyward, releasing communities from generational pain. Quorilith established Library of Shifting Sigils, pages rewriting as reader learns, ensuring knowledge remains living. Dra goons and monks consulted during strategems, discovering tactical manuals morphing when motive shifted from defense to conquest, forcing introspection. Thalxior created Paradox Forum within Vale of Concord, inviting Mirrorsages, crimson agents, soldiers to debate impossible dilemmas. Forum ranked responses by coherence rather than correctness, cultivating leaders adept at navigating ambiguity. Seraphon opened Gate of Gentle Departures at Argent threshold, guiding souls whose last act resonated with authenticity, regardless of virtue. A murderer who confessed truth might cross before hypocrite king whose lies rotted crown. Emergent mortal orders aligned with each archon site. Courage Circle of Ember Guardians, Balanced Hands Consortium, Crystal Pact Brokers, Lament Choristers, Sigil Navigators, Paradox Mediators, Threshold Guides. Each order blended classes cooperatively, demonstrating microcosm of lattice ideals.

SOUL_CHARTER.verbatim: Conclave agreed to pilot program in Avernus front lines. Soul Warden Innorbatos presented charter to legion deserters, offering protection in exchange for eternal service with explicit statement that freedom never regained. Some accepted, seeing offer as honest anchor in chaotic war. When charter sealed, lattice pulsed, not in condemnation, but with somber note, recognizing authentic submission. Devils exulted until vision revealed souls glowing dim, energy yield lower than deceit harvested souls. Asmodeus realised sincerity curbed despair, reducing nutritional value for Hell. Plan considered unsustainable. Simultaneously Crimson Accord shuddered. Demons sensed devils flirting with authenticity and erupted in outrage, for chaos realm defines itself by rejection of coherent narrative. Ul nak stirred in distant dream, whispering through Abyssal storms, promising power to any legion that shattered lattice. Tanar ri warbands swarmed infernal border, screaming truths of raw impulse, blades coated with madness. The sentient Pact responded by wrapping battlefield with shimmering veil that manifested each combatant true desire as visible flame trailing movements. Soldiers saw own motive writ large, fear or lust or hatred or love. Some halted, disgusted. Others fought harder, proud of flame. Casualty patterns shifted unpredictably.

DEATH_CHANGE.path: The Decennium Descent and the Matrix of Oblivion.docx
DEATH_CHANGE.verbatim: Here, death is not the greatest danger. Death remains a change from one state to another and therefore still produces resonance.

CESSATION.path: The Decennium Descent and the Matrix of Oblivion.docx
CESSATION.verbatim: The greater threat is cessation without transition: the removal of desire, reaction, memory, spirit, and consequence until nothing remains that can be said to have changed.

WARDEN_PURPOSE.path: The Decennium Descent and the Matrix of Oblivion.docx
WARDEN_PURPOSE.verbatim: Its purpose is to maintain the resonance cycle, prevent unauthorized access to the deepest seal, regulate the opening and closing of the dungeon, and ensure that no faction—celestial, infernal, mortal, or otherwise—gains permanent control of the descent.

WARDEN_SYSTEM.path: The Decennium Descent and the Matrix of Oblivion.docx
WARDEN_SYSTEM.verbatim: A massacre at the entrance may be permissible if it produces no threat to the prison. A peaceful occupation may provoke immediate intervention if it begins reducing the dungeon’s necessary instability.

INFERNAL_CLAUSES.path: The Decennium Descent and the Matrix of Oblivion.docx
INFERNAL_CLAUSES.verbatim: Infernal powers trade in soul coins, bargains, resurrection clauses, and contracts written to remain enforceable even after the dungeon seals.

MORTAL_TESTIMONY.verbatim: The beliefs recorded in this appendix are mortal theology, not objective cosmic history. Priests, scholars, and cults across Aethel have spent millennia reasoning about forces they cannot fully perceive. What follows is what the faithful believe: a creation myth, a pantheon of worshiped faces, and a diagram of the planes — sincerely held, widely taught, and useful for understanding how ordinary people in Aethel think about the divine. Your character may treat this as literal truth. Deeper mysteries of the Spiral and the Crucible may surface only through play; even then, the wider world does not rewrite its temples overnight. Scholars may also speak of the First Choir — seven named virtues (Korvelan, Vaerilune, Delvaran, Shaelara, Xalarex, Thalirion, and Virellian) — as part of the wider Spiral story. That knowledge is not secret, but it is not tavern talk either.

SHADOW_CLAIMS.verbatim: The Veiled Expanse is dominated by the Shadow Conclave, a loose alliance of powerful entities who have claimed dominion over different aspects of shadow, death, and darkness. Unlike the Fey Courts or Elemental Courts, the Shadow Conclave operates more like a council of equals, each member respecting the others' territories while pursuing their own agendas.

SHADOW_AGENTS.verbatim: The Shadow Conclave rarely acts in unison, but when faced with threats to the Veiled Expanse itself, they can combine their considerable powers to devastating effect. Their agents often work in the Material Plane, collecting souls, spreading darkness, or maintaining the balance between life and death.

RESEARCH_REQUIREMENTS.verbatim: Ordinary spell research can be completed with Arcana and a laboratory. Matrix research cannot. The primary researcher must personally possess high ranks in multiple disciplines—Arcana, History, Religion, Nature, and Engineering—and must cross-reference rare drops, libraries, mechanisms, and seasonal changes. Archive knowledge may be inherited; cognitive continuity usually cannot.

FORBIDDEN_MAGIC.verbatim: Forbidden is a legal, religious, or metaphysical classification, not a universal school. Soul destruction, involuntary identity alteration, Old One contact, permanent Gate rewriting, Unity resonance, and Matrical execution are forbidden because their consequences exceed the target. Casting such magic can create evidence, attention, Pact pursuit, or changes to the dungeon even when the spell succeeds.

RETURN_CONSEQUENCES.verbatim: Resurrection restores life but does not automatically remove Wounds, Corruption, debt, legal death, or claims upon the recovered body.

CAPABILITY_RESPECT.verbatim: Resurrection and death prevention. Use access, time, body recovery, faction law, and what returns with the character as story questions. Do not arbitrarily switch abilities off.

VISIBLE_BARGAINS.verbatim: Write important terms down. State what each side believes the wording means and what mechanism or witness enforces it. Allow players to exploit language when they earned the interpretation, but give intelligent NPCs the same opportunity. Do not spring clauses that no character could perceive or understand.

MULTIPLE_CLUES.verbatim: Place one clue in the environment, one in an NPC or rival relationship, one in a recoverable record, and one in the behavior of the tier’s hazards. The Expedition should be able to assemble the truth from different team contributions. This is where the twelve-seat structure earns its place: Combat may hold the approach, Reconnaissance finds the seam, Research reads the sequence, Resource prepares the material, and Support keeps the ritual intact.

value.name: Stitch Fate

operational.targets: One living dying creature at 0 HP you can perceive within range and line of effect. Dead and Stable creatures are ineligible.
operational.resolution: Choose one mode before paying. Unravel Failure requires at least one recorded failed death save and removes one failure. Stitch Life clears death-save counters and restores 1 HP as direct state recovery.
operational.effect: Unravel Failure leaves the creature dying at 0 HP with its other recorded successes/failures intact. Stitch Life restores a living dying creature to 1 HP, ending its zero-HP dying state. If a broad cannot-regain-HP effect blocks that 1 HP, instead clear its death counters, make it Stable at 0, and roll its ordinary d4-hour recovery deadline from now. A still-active HP prohibition can defer that eventual recovery; damage or death cancels it normally.
operational.scaling: None. The spell changes only one recorded failure or the defined 1-HP state recovery.
operational.limitations: An Action cannot interrupt or retroactively change a completed death. This is not resurrection or ordinary HP healing; ordinary healing bonuses/halves do not alter the 1-HP state value. It removes no Wounds, Corruption, class Curse, conditions, debt or spent-resource consequences. Normal class access, RP, Dissonance, Refrain, components and countering rules apply. No refund after a legally paid cast is countered or fails at resolution.
operational.designNotes: Core Divination rank8, 21RP, Action, 120ft, V/S/F and Instantaneous are preserved. Source says change one failed death save or auto-revive a dying target. NEW: two explicit modes; recorded-failure removal instead of a retroactive reroll; living-dying eligibility; 1-HP state recovery and blocked-recovery Stable bridge. Reviewed operational playtest overlay; provisional design decisions remain labeled NEW.

value.name: Death Ward

operational.targets: One living creature you can perceive within range and line of effect
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute; ends when its prevention is used
operational.resolution: No initial save. While the spell remains active, the first eligible effect that would reduce the target from positive HP to 0 without Core Instant Death or another outright-death result instead leaves it at 1 HP; then the ward ends.
operational.effect: Prevent one positive-to-zero HP crossing. Preserve the raw damage packet, Core Instant Death check, half-maximum/Maiming Wound triggers and attached conditions. The prevented positive-to-zero crossing does not itself create a drop-only Wound save. This is loss prevention, not healing, so a cannot-regain-HP effect does not stop it. Other eligible survival effects are rechecked after the selected prevention resolves; no duplicate automatic use is consumed after the crossing has already been prevented.
operational.scaling: None. Always one eligible crossing and a 1-HP floor.
operational.limitations: Does not trigger while the target is already at 0. Does not resurrect, repair a vital body, prevent third death-save failure/fatal Wound death/lethal-track death or override explicitly unpreventable HP loss. Cannot legalize an otherwise unaffordable HP cost. If multiple independently owned wards exist, use only the chosen eligible prevention; unused records retain their own concentration/deadline. This is distinct from Cleric Ritual of Undeath's would-die replacement. Normal spell costs and risk apply.
operational.designNotes: Core Necromancy rank4, 7RP, Action, 60ft and concentration1minute retained with exact class gates. M/F uses the already-reviewed class-focus alternative; no unstated material cost. NEW: living target, explicit positive crossing, outright-death exclusion and competing-prevention procedure. The agreed damage/HP-loss interface is in the candidate guide; reviewed for the operational playtest overlay.

value.name: Resurrection

operational.targets: One willing dead creature whose sufficiently intact remains are within range and line of effect, and whose death occurred no more than 8 elapsed hours ago
operational.resolution: No attack or save. Check the dead identity's willingness, sufficient body, exact elapsed death window, location and actual resurrection/soul blockers. On a legal successful resolution, return that identity to life at 1 HP.
operational.effect: Change Dead to Living, assign 1 returned HP, clear death-save counters and any previous Stable recovery deadline. Preserve Wounds, Corruption, Oracle Curse, other persistent death consequences and spent resources. This returned HP is a resurrection state transition, not ordinary healing; ordinary healing reductions and generic living HP-gain prohibitions do not change it. Explicit resurrection or soul blockers prevent return.
operational.scaling: None. One identity returns at 1 HP; no additional targets or restored resources.
operational.limitations: Does not create a missing viable body, duplicate a creature, compel an unwilling return, bypass a real planar/soul barrier, clear lethal tracks or repair otherwise lethal persistent afflictions. After successful return, retain Exhaustion6/Expedition6 and enter their protected living-collapse states. Later positive unprevented gain is lethal again; qualifying care and point gates still apply. This candidate remains reviewed for the operational playtest overlay. Known illegal prerequisites prevent activation; a legal cast already paid receives no refund for a later refusal, counter or changed eligibility. Normal RP, Dissonance, Refrain and component rules apply.
operational.designNotes: Core Necromancy rank7, 17RP, Action, 120ft, V/S/F and Instantaneous retained. Class gates remain Cleric/Druid/Wizard13 and Shaman19. NEW provisional design: one target, willingness/body/line requirements, eight-hour elapsed window and1 returned HP. No imported diamond cost or hour-long cast. Any other remains of this identity lose eligibility to create a second living instance; they remain mundane remains/history evidence as appropriate. # Healing, survival and resurrection — playtest interface

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED — selected scope only.** The [final notebook review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_HEALING_FINAL_CLOSURE.md) closes147 classified class passages plus6 individually reviewed ordinary spell objects. Those6 spells are now operational playtest drafts; the catalog has78 operational and770 unfinished entries. This is a bounded interface, not DD24 completion:131 additional semantic matches and healing content in other domains still need dispositions. Original cards/books are preserved.

[Exact source procedures](HEALING_DEATH_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) · [Latest boundary decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_HEALING_FINAL_BOUNDARIES.md) · [Supplement decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_HEALING_SUPPLEMENT_REVIEW.md) · [Reference checks](HEALING_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json) · [Source integrity](HEALING_DEATH_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json)

## Distinct life operations

| Operation | Result | Restriction interface |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum-HP prevention | Preserve positiveHP instead of crossing a floor | Not HP gain; cannot create positiveHP from0 |
| Ordinary healing | Increase a living creature's normalHP | Apply modifiers, prohibitions, reserve and Critical ceiling |
| Direct state recovery | Specifically defined dying/Stable/HP recovery | Broad cannot-regain-HP applies; ordinary healing modifiers do not |
| Would-die replacement | Replace a pending death before it becomes final | Exact source eligibility; not a generic damage floor |
| Resurrection | Actually dead willing identity returns at printedHP | Separate life transition; actual corpse/soul blockers apply |
| Companion reconstruction | Restore a device/companion through its own source | No general creature resurrection permission |
| TemporaryHP | Separate nonstacking buffer | Not healing, stabilization or resurrection |

Names never select the operation. Phoenix Rebirth heals a still-living ally at0. Cleric Resurrection returns an actual dead identity. Ritual of Undeath's Ward replaces death; ordinary Death Ward is a positive-to-zero floor. Feign death and spirit manifestations are not death or resurrection.

## Damage quantities and resolution

| Quantity | Definition and use |
|---|---|
| resolvedDamage | After defenses, before tempHP; positive damage event iff greater than0 |
| tempAbsorbed | min(tempHP, resolvedDamage) |
| postTempDamage | resolvedDamage minus tempAbsorbed, uncapped by currentHP; Core Instant Death/Wounds |
| actualHpDamage | NormalHP lost to the packet after true prevention; recovery and state-assignment loss excluded |
| actualDamageDealt | NEW anti-overkill bridge: tempAbsorbed plus actualHpDamage; numeric actual-damage drains/reflections |

Ordinary “damages,” “takes damage” and “damaging hit” predicates use a positive resolved packet. Actual-HP wording (Burning Blood/Rewind Wound) uses actualHpDamage. Numeric actual-damage wording (Sanguine Rite/Echo Leech/Merciful Smite/Wound Eater/Gravebrand) uses actualDamageDealt. Source attack/hit predicates remain distinct.

Example: HP10/temp10 takes5: numeric actual damage5, actualHP damage0, positive packet. HP1 under a floor takes5: numeric0 but positive packet. HP3 takes12: numeric3, raw post-temp12. HP0 takes1: numeric0, positive packet and normal death-failure consequences.

Divine Judgment consumes its once-this-actual-target-turn entitlement on a positive packet, then reflects min(Cleric level, max(1, floor(actualDamageDealt/2))). Thus HP1-floor/numeric0 reflects1 and consumes; fully prevented resolved0 does neither. Wrathful Brand/Balanced Scales use the positive predicate where their source says damage occurred.

Resolve a damage event in this order:

1. Snapshot pre-event HP/tempHP/Wounds; resolve defenses, temp absorption and uncapped post-temp damage.
2. Core Instant Death uses postTempDamage minus preHP greater than or equal to effective maximum when reduced to0. It precedes ordinary floors. Open a legal would-die replacement; stop that packet's death procedure. No Wound save or zero-HP failure follows this branch.
3. If not Instant Death, resolve applicable true floors. They cannot raise an already0 creature. They preserve raw damage and attached conditions; a prevented drop creates no drop-only Wound trigger, but half-max/Maiming still applies.
4. Spiral-TouchedIII alone has a specific pre-Wound recovery exception. If positive-to-zero remains, spend its use, preserve that raw crossing trigger, attempt quarter-max direct recovery and apply phase-out. Broad HP-gain prohibition blocks the recovery but not the use/phase.
5. Resolve the one Core Wound save using original post-temp damage and pre-event Wounds. Fatal Wound death opens its own legal replacement window. Actual death ends Spiral phase; a successful independent Ward prevents actual death.
6. Resolve already-zero damage failures/death and its legal replacement window. A successful replacement stops skipped same-packet death branches; never replay a Wound/failure branch merely because replacement changedHP.
7. Finalize a newly surviving0 creature's dying/Stable/knockout state. Only an explicitly triggered post-zero Reaction such as Grace Reversal can act before ordinary zeroHP Reaction loss finalizes.
8. Resolve eligible post-zero Phoenix/Unyielding-style healing only if target still lives, followed by later triggers. This healing never retroactively reduces the triggering packet's numeric damage.

The affected creature chooses among simultaneously eligible offered survival effects, then rechecks remaining triggers. A paid Reaction spends its declared cost; a limited automatic survival use spends when its actual source resolves. A true floor preventing the crossing means Spiral's use is not spent. No generic extra Reaction or return from death is created.

For Ritual Ward, sufficient body and no explicitly unpreventable death are prerequisites. It can intercept Instant Death, fatal Wounds, third death-save failure, eligible direct death and lethal tracks. Positive pre-eventHP→1 is loss prevention and works through Decay. Already0 with HP gain prohibited instead becomes living Stable0: clear counters and establish a d4-hour recovery deadline immediately.

Freeze packetHpLossBeforeReplacement after true floors but before Ward. Ward metrics are min(packetHpLossBeforeReplacement, max(0, preHP minus replacementHP)); never include loss caused solely by assigning a lowerHP state. HP20 takes10 then fatal Wound/Ward1 means actualHP damage10, not19. HP5 takes100 then Ward1 means actualHP damage4, raw100.

Direct death (e.g. Wound EaterIII) produces no damage or Wound save. Its healing requires actual death; a Ward interception prevents that trigger without refunding the paid activation. False LifeI has only its printed floor and failed-death-save replacement modes sharing1/LR; it is not an all-causes Ward.

## ZeroHP permissions and start timing

A conscious but dying creature still rolls at each regular start unless Stable. Extra turns do not advance these regular-start deadlines. Further damage and actual death retain normal consequences.

Mage Undying Spellform partially overrides only zeroHP Unconscious/Incapacitated restrictions: normal speech, voluntary half-Speed movement, normal Action, legal spellcasting with that Action, and starting/maintaining concentration. No independent BA/Reaction. Existing concentration avoids automatic loss from zeroHP, but the triggering damage still requires its concentration save. Separate Stunned/Unconscious/Expedition5 or6/Silence and other restrictions still apply. Healing above0 ends the feature. Expiry at0 destabilizes, cancels the Stable recovery deadline and adds one failure; the third kills normally and permits only an eligible would-die replacement.

Oracle False LifeIII permits exactly one choice during the allowed zeroHP turn: move up to Speed, speak, or activate one Revelation. The latter uses its printed Action/BA/trigger (trigger must occur on that turn), costs and components. It can start concentration; the feature did not preserve earlier concentration. No independent actions accompany the choice.

False LifeV quarter-max direct recovery resolves at its next regular start before the death save. Blocked recovery leaves0 without invented stability; dead creatures do not revive. Spiral phase expires at its next regular start before normal start processing. Fate-BoundIV rerolls a failed death save before committing natural1/counters; use the new result. Its generic death-effect save bonus is not an ordinary death-save modifier. A natural20 whose1HP is blocked uses the previously reviewed Decay bridge: Stable0, cleared counters, immediate d4-hour deadline and preserved used-turn marker. It does not spend Ward. This differs from blocked False LifeV, which remains dying.

## Ordinary healing arithmetic

Determine legal source, recipients, costs, clocks and available entitlements before arithmetic. The helper receives already eligible modifiers; it does not acquire class powers or validate every source for its caller.

Pre-resolution modifiers include Words of Equilibrium's formula M, Zealot's Fervor +S, Throne's Grace +1/die capped S+M, Benevolent Spirits' eligible paid-technique +M, Life Prophecy maximizing dice, and Crane's applicable +S. Conditional add-ons include Ground, Radiance, Aura of Faith, Ember Mantle, Life Linked's rolled1d4, Ranger Healing Touch, Aura of Mercy, Garden's stored+1 and Tranquil Lotus Step.

# Unity and False Resonance — Director Canon

## Unity

**Unity** is false resonance: a counterfeit harmony created not by distinct voices acting together, but by removing meaningful distinction until alternatives disappear.

It can present itself through compassion, efficiency, prosperity, security, peace, equality, order, or collective purpose. None of those ideals is inherently corrupt. The danger begins when a system makes disagreement, exit, independent identity, or genuine alternative impossible.

True resonance preserves difference. False resonance consumes it.

Unity attacks the Matrix by collapsing:

**Difference → Conflict → Motion → History → Memory → Identity → Will**

The end state is not peaceful civilization. It is a zero-state in which nothing meaningfully chooses, differs, becomes, remembers, or wants.

Goblins are metaphysically **more susceptible to Unity than most mortal peoples**. This is a vulnerability, not a moral alignment.

- susceptibility is not guilt;
- many goblins are unaffected;
- some goblins identify and oppose Unity more fiercely than anyone else;

These institutions can generate true resonance through risk and competing choice—or become false-resonance vectors when participation hardens into dependency and alternatives disappear.

## Moloch and the Coinfather Pattern

Moloch did not invent goblin commerce and is not secretly behind every bank, contract, or war. He exploits existing systems.

The Coinfather pattern converts:

- value into surveillance;
- obligation into identity;
- prosperity into dependency;
- voluntary exchange into a structure from which meaningful exit becomes impossible.

A small number of financiers knowingly serve Moloch. Many more can reproduce parts of the pattern without understanding what they are doing.

Use this pattern sparingly. Ordinary greed, ordinary debt, ordinary corruption, and ordinary war must continue to exist independently or Unity becomes an explanation for everything and therefore explains nothing.

## The Ancient Anti-Goblin Crusade

The crusade is intentionally morally difficult.

Crusader records describe cult penetration, captured institutions, weaponized debt, expanding promises of compulsory peace, and a civilization-scale false-resonance threat. They may have correctly identified a genuine existential vector and may have believed eradication was the only reliable containment method available.

Goblin histories describe extermination, dispossession, collective punishment, and the destruction of communities that had no knowledge of Unity and in many cases opposed the implicated institutions.

Both bodies of evidence contain truth.

The setting should not force a clean answer that the crusade was either pure heroism or meaningless bigotry. The question it leaves Directors and players is harder: **how does a civilization respond to a real risk that is unevenly distributed among a people without converting susceptibility into collective guilt?**
